title: Extraction and Electron Microscopy Visualization of Lipids in Viburnum tinus Fruit
author: Sinnott-Armstrong, Vignolini, et al.

steps.title: Configure Cryo‑Ultramicrotome System
steps.instruction: In a well‑ventilated microtome room equipped with an oxygen sensor, remove the knife support and armrest from the Ultracut UC6, mount the FC7 cryochamber, switch on the main power and activate the FC7 option, connect the chamber to a liquid‑nitrogen tank, mount a 35° diamond knife and cryo‑trimming tool on a rotating knife holder, place the holder on a knife plate inside the chamber, insert a specimen holder with a flat clamp into the specimen arm, position an antistatic electrode in the chamber and power it, start cooling to reach –90 °C for knife and gas and –110 °C for the specimen (≈30–40 min), and keep ambient conditions at ~22 °C, 60 % RH (no thermal cycler needed).

substeps.instruction: Remove knife support and armrest from Ultracut UC6.
Mount FC7 cryochamber to Ultracut UC6.
Switch on main power and activate FC7 control option.
Connect cryochamber to liquid‑nitrogen tank.
Mount 35° diamond knife and cryo‑trimming tool on rotating knife holder.
Place rotating knife holder on knife plate inside cryochamber.
Insert specimen holder with flat clamp into specimen arm.
Place antistatic electrode in cryochamber and switch on its power.
Cool chamber: target –90 °C (knife & gas), –110 °C (specimen); 30–40 min.
Ambient ~22 °C, 60 % RH; no thermal cycler used.

steps.title: Glow Discharge Carbon‑Coated Grid
steps.instruction: Glow‑discharge a carbon‑coated 200‑mesh copper grid (e.g., EMS Cat# CF200‑Cu or index grid Cat# G200F1‑Cu) at 15 mA for 25 s using a glow discharger; ensure dry air or nitrogen supply is available for recovery of cryo‑sections, adding a nitrogen tank with regulator if needed.

substeps.instruction: Place carbon‑coated 200‑mesh copper grid in glow discharger.
Set current to 15 mA and discharge for 25 s.
Confirm availability of dry air or N₂ for section recovery; add N₂ tank with regulator if absent.

steps.title: Prepare Reflux Extractor
steps.instruction: Under a fume hood, place the reflux extractor, connect water lines to its condensers, add ~50 mL chloroform and a few boiling stones to the solvent container, position the container at the extractor base, start circulating cooling water, and heat the solvent with a sand bath to ≈80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Put reflux extractor under fume hood and connect water lines to condensers.
Add ~50 mL chloroform and a few boiling stones to the solvent container.
Place solvent container at the bottom of the extractor.
Start cooling‑water circulation in condensers.
Heat solvent with sand bath to about 80 °C.

steps.title: Cryo‑Fix Fruit Epicarp
steps.instruction: Pour liquid nitrogen into a stainless‑steel Dewar, cool a ~5 mL container (e.g., lower half of a 15 mL centrifuge tube with brass wire handle) in the LN₂ bath, then fill it with ethane gas and allow it to liquefy.

substeps.instruction: Pour liquid nitrogen into a stainless‑steel Dewar.
Place lower half of a ~5 mL container in LN₂ and let it reach LN₂ temperature.
Fill the cooled container with ethane gas and allow it to liquidize.

steps.title: Mount Epicarp on Carbon‑Coated Filter Paper
steps.instruction: Peel the pericarp with a razor blade, blot excess juice quickly with filter paper (thickness 100–200 µm, remove flesh), cut the epicarp into a ~3 mm × 1 mm strip and a filter‑paper strip ~5 mm × 3 mm, spread graphite adhesive on half of the filter paper, place the epicarp so its lower half contacts the half‑dried carbon paste, let the paste dry, and hold the assembly with cross‑locked tweezers (melt solid ethane by touching with room‑temperature tweezers if needed).

substeps.instruction: Peel pericarp with razor blade; blot excess juice with filter paper (minimize time).
Note epicarp thickness 100–200 µm; remove as much flesh as possible.
Cut epicarp strip ≈3 mm (L) × 1 mm (W).
Cut filter‑paper strip ≈5 mm (L) × 3 mm (W).
Spread carbon adhesive paste on half of the filter‑paper strip.
Place epicarp on edge of filter paper so only lower half contacts half‑dried carbon paste.
Allow carbon paste to dry and ensure firm adhesion.
Hold the filter‑paper part with cross‑locked tweezers.
If ethane solidifies in LN₂, melt it by touching with room‑temperature tweezers.

steps.title: Quench Specimen in Liquid Ethane
steps.instruction: Immerse the assembled specimen in liquid ethane for ~10 s to vitrify, then transfer the frozen block to a polystyrene container filled with liquid nitrogen for storage until ultramicrotomy.

substeps.instruction: Quench specimen in liquid ethane for about 10 seconds.
Transfer frozen specimen to liquid nitrogen in a polystyrene container for storage.

steps.title: Cut Ultrathin Sections on EM Grids
steps.instruction: Using the prepared cryo‑ultramicrotome (knife at –90 °C, specimen at –110 °C), trim and cut ultrathin cryo‑sections of the frozen epicarp and collect them onto the glow‑discharged carbon‑coated EM grids.

steps.title: Acquire Pre‑Extraction TEM Image
steps.instruction: Insert each grid into a transmission electron microscope, use low‑dose imaging conditions, and record the region of interest as the “before” image.

steps.title: Perform Lipid Extraction with Refluxed Chloroform
steps.instruction: Place the grid on a filter‑paper strip, set the strip on the extractor’s sample holder, insert the holder into the reflux extractor and tilt it ≈20° so condensed chloroform flows down, then expose the grid to refluxed chloroform for 10–20 min, ensuring continuous flow of liquid chloroform across the specimen.

substeps.instruction: Put the grid on a filter‑paper strip.
Place the strip on the extractor’s sample holder.
Insert holder into extractor and tilt ≈20° to direct condensed chloroform downwards.
Treat grid with refluxed chloroform for 10–20 minutes, maintaining flow.

steps.title: Acquire Post‑Extraction TEM Image and Compare
steps.instruction: Remove the grid, let it air‑dry, re‑insert it into the TEM, image the same area under identical low‑dose conditions, and compare image contrast to the pre‑extraction view to assess lipid loss.

substeps.instruction: Remove grid from extractor and let dry in air.
Insert dried grid into TEM.
Image the same field under the same low‑dose settings.
Compare contrast with the before image; reduced contrast indicates lipid loss.
